**Chicago Fire and Portland Timbers kick off a heavyweight tilt at Soldier Field** — both teams have won 3 of their last 5, so expect a sharp, competitive affair. 🔥

Fire have depth problems on the injury front but just beat Charlotte at home, while the Timbers are rolling with back-to-back wins and look razor-sharp in transition. The H2H is remarkably tight: Chicago's only grabbed 1 win in the last 10 meetings, but draws have been the norm.

Key storylines:

- **J. Bamba and P. Zinckernagel** lead Chicago's attack, but they'll need to be clinical without A. Franco in the lineup
- **Portland's midfield balance** — D. Da Costa and J. Caicedo have been solid anchors, and the Timbers' set-up should control possession
- Home-field advantage could matter here; Fire's recent form at Soldier Field gives them a slight edge despite injury headaches

Expected lineups:

- **Chicago Fire**: C. Brady, V. Radojević, J. Elliott, A. Gutman, L. Barroso, A. Salétros, D. T. D'Avilla, J. Dean, M. Haile-Selassie, P. Zinckernagel, J. Bamba
- **Portland Timbers**: J. Pantemis, K. Velde, F. Surman, J. Fory, B. Bye, D. Da Costa, J. Caicedo, A. Alves, C. Bassett, A. Lassiter, K. Kelsy

Prediction:

**1-1 draw** leans likely — history favors stalemate, and both teams' recent form suggests they'll cancel each other out. Could easily go either way. ⚽

**NYCFC host the Union in a battle of inconsistency versus hot form** — the hosts are limping through a five-game stretch while Philly's rolling. 🔥

NYCFC have drawn too much lately and are dealing with a brutal injury pile-up. The Union, by contrast, have won three of their last five and just dismantled the Red Bulls 3-1 at home. Philly's got serious momentum heading into the Bronx.

Key storylines:

- **NYCFC's injury crisis** — five players out including O'Neill and Martínez leaves the attack thin. **Ojeda** and **Magno** need to step up big.
- **Philadelphia's attack is humming** — **Damiani** and **Iloski** have been clinical finishing. The Union's defensive record speaks volumes lately.
- **H2H momentum matters** — Philly owns the last decade at 6-4, so this isn't neutral ground despite the venue.

Expected lineups:

- **New York City FC**: Freese, Cavallo, Martins, Gray, Carrizo, Perea, Shore, Jones, Wolf, Ojeda, Magno
- **Philadelphia Union**: Rick, Westfield, Blake, Martínez, Harriel, Vassilev, Jean Jacques, Lukić, Sullivan, Iloski, Damiani

Prediction:

**Philadelphia 2-1 New York City** — the Union are the slight favorite here. Better form, fewer gaps in the squad, and they've historically had NYCFC's number.

**Corinthians host a flying Cruzeiro side in a battle of form.** This is the kind of Sunday night clash where the in-form visitor (3W in last 5) can absolutely punish a wavering home team. 🔥

Corinthians have steadied the ship with back-to-back wins, but injuries are piling up across the defensive line. Cruzeiro, meanwhile, are on a **three-game winning streak** and looking sharp — expect them to test that creaky Corinthians backline relentlessly.

Key storylines:

- **G. Paulista and G. Henrique** anchoring Corinthians' defense will face a relentless attack from **K. Arroyo and K. Jorge** in Cruzeiro's front three
- **J. Lingard's** creativity in midfield becomes even more vital with Corinthians stretched thin at the back
- Cruzeiro's **Gerson** controlling the tempo from deep — this could be the difference-maker if Corinthians can't find rhythm early

Expected lineups:

- **Corinthians**: H. Souza, Matheuzinho, G. Paulista, G. Henrique, M. Bidu, B. Bidon, Raniele, J. Lingard, R. Garro, G. Negão
- **Cruzeiro**: Otávio, Kaiki, J. Jesus, F. Bruno, K. Moraes, M. Pereira, Gerson, Wesley, K. Arroyo, K. Jorge

Prediction:

**Cruzeiro 2-1 Corinthians.** The visitor's momentum and Corinthians' defensive fragility point to a Cruzeiro edge here. 📍

**Courage looking sharp and hungry; Dash trying to shake off a sluggish stretch.** North Carolina's rolling with three wins in their last five and are absolutely **clinical at home** — that 5-0 demolition of Orlando was serious business. Houston's been treading water (1W, 3D in their last five) and haven't found their rhythm yet. 🔥

The head-to-head leans Courage's way (5-4-1), and with **Courage's offensive firepower** vs **Dash's defensive fragility**, this feels like a mismatch on paper.

Key storylines:

- **Courage's attack** needs to keep its ruthless streak going — **E. Ijeh** and **L. Thompson** have been clinical finishers
- **Dash middleeld control** through **M. Graham** and **D. Colaprico** will be critical to slow North Carolina's tempo
- **Home advantage** at WakeMed is real; Courage are a different beast there

Expected lineups:

- **North Carolina Courage**: K. Sheridan, F. Rauch, M. Bell, U. Shiragaki, R. Williams, R. Jackson, D. Weatherholt, M. Matsukubo, A. Sanchez, L. Thompson, E. Ijeh
- **Houston Dash**: J. Campbell, L. Boattin, L. M. Klenke, P. Nielsen, A. Patterson, M. Graham, D. Colaprico, K. v. Zanten, L. Ullmark, K. Faasse, K. A. Rader

Prediction:

**Courage 2–0 Dash.** North Carolina's the clear favorite here — sharper form, home turf, and Houston just hasn't found gear yet.

**América rolls in as the form horse, and Atlético San Luis is short two key pieces — this should be a lopsided affair at the Azteca.** 🏟️

América's 3W-1D-1L start is legit, complete with a **dominant 3-0 win over Santos**. San Luis, meanwhile, are mixing decent results (2W-2D) but got torched 2-3 by Cruz Azul and are without two of their main attacking weapons.

Key storylines:

- **P. Salas** leading América's attack with fresh legs, facing a San Luis backline stretched thin by injuries
- América's midfield engines **E. Sánchez** and **A. Zendejas** controlling possession against a San Luis side that draws a lot (2D in last 5)
- San Luis desperate for a road point with **C. Lopez** and **João Pedro Galvão** sidelined — their depth is being tested hard

Expected lineups:

- **Club América**: R. Cota, C. Borja, M. Vázquez, R. Juárez, D. Espinoza, E. Sánchez, A. Zendejas, H. Martín, I. Violante, R. Zúñiga, P. Salas
- **Atlético San Luis**: A. Sánchez, R. Bambu, E. Águila, M. A. García, R. Torres, O. Macías, S. Salles-Lamonge, S. P. Bouquet, A. Duarte, D. Rodriguez, L. Flores

Prediction:

**América 2-0 San Luis.** At home with form and a talent edge, this leans heavily toward a comfortable host W. 📍

**Central Córdoba's home form is fragile, and Instituto's hot streak could be the perfect antidote.** 🔥 This Córdoba derby is shaping up as a classic momentum clash — one team desperately needing a win at home, the other clicking on all cylinders.

Central Córdoba has wobbled at the Terrera with just one win in their last five, while Instituto De Córdoba arrives unbeaten in their last four games. The visiting side's defensive setup (3-4-2) should give Central's front line fits, especially with **L. González** and **M. Santos** tasked with breaking down a stubborn shape.

Key storylines:

- **Instituto's winning streak** puts pressure on Central to snap a three-game skid and reclaim home advantage
- **Central Córdoba's head-to-head edge** (2-1 in last three meetings) offers some comfort, but form trumps history right now
- **The midfield battle** between Central's **T. Cravero** and **J. Cardozo** against Instituto's **G. Abregú** and **D. Sosa** could decide possession flow

Expected lineups:

- **Central Córdoba**: J. Vallejos, D. Barrera, A. Maciel, F. Mansilla, F. Martínez, M. Vera, T. Cravero, J. Cardozo, L. González, M. Santos, E. Naya
- **Instituto De Córdoba**: M. Ledesma, L. Mosevich, F. Alarcón, A. Massaccesi, G. Cerato, D. Sosa, G. Abregú, J. Lázaro, M. Gallardo, A. Luna, J. Córdoba

Prediction:

**Instituto De Córdoba 1–0 Central Córdoba**. Instituto's form and organization gives them the edge. 📍

**Barracas hosting Rosario in a battle of contrasting form — one's hot, the other's steadier, but the away side's got pedigree.** 🔥

Barracas are flying (3 wins in their last 5), while Rosario sit middle-of-the-road with a draw against Corinthians and that statement win over River. The head-to-head favors Rosario 2-1, but Barracas are unbeaten at home in this run and won't roll over.

Key storylines:

- **Barracas' attack** — **J. Candia** and **F. Bruera** have been clinical; they'll need to stay sharp against a Rosario defence missing firepower depth due to injuries.

- **Rosario's midfield anchor** — **F. Ibarra** and **Á. Di María** will be crucial to controlling tempo and limiting Barracas' home press.

- **Injury toll on Rosario** — **F. Cervi**, **J. Giménez**, and **M. Rubén** out; depth will be tested, especially if the match tightens.

Expected lineups:

- **Barracas Central**: M. A. Miño, N. Demartini, K. Jappert, N. Capraro, R. Insúa, F. Tobio, I. Tapia, T. Porra, D. Miloc, J. Candia, F. Bruera

- **Rosario Central**: C. Ledesma, G. Ávila, I. Ovando, E. Coronel, A. Sández, F. Ibarra, Á. Di María, E. Copetti, V. Pizarro, G. Cantizano, T. Badaloni

Prediction:

**Barracas 1-1 Rosario**. Home-field heat meets away composure — coin flip between a fired-up host and a wounded visitor.

**A Texas derby where Austin needs to bounce back fast** — the hosts are reeling from consecutive away losses and can't afford another slip-up at home. 🔥

Austin's been all over the map: dominant at the Estadio one moment, getting thumped 0-3 the next. FC Dallas, meanwhile, are the steadier outfit lately, grinding out results (2W-2D) and sitting tighter defensively. The missing bodies pile up worse for Dallas, though — five players out is a proper squad hit.

Key storylines:

- **Austin FC's home form** is their last lifeline after back-to-back road disasters; Q2 Stadium should be a fortress moment.
- **FC Dallas injury crisis** forces creative lineups; depth gets tested hard without Julio, Daniel, and Ramiro.
- **B. Vázquez and M. Uzuni** spearheading Austin's attack will need to finish clinical chances — no margin for waste at home.

Expected lineups:

- **Austin FC**: B. Stuver, Guilherme Biro, J. Rosales, M. Đorđević, J. Gallagher, O. Svatok, F. Torres, E. Torres, M. Uzuni, C. Ramirez, B. Vázquez
- **FC Dallas**: M. Collodi, S. Moore, O. Urhoghide, S. Ibeagha, J. Valiente, R. Binyamin, Kaick, P. Delgado, H. Johansson, P. Musa, L. Farrington

Prediction:

**Austin FC 2–1 FC Dallas** — home advantage + Dallas's injury pile-up gives the Crew a slight edge. 📍

**Angel City's looking to bounce back in front of their home crowd, but Washington Spirit come in hot with three wins in their last five.** 🔥 This opener has all the makings of a proper scrap.

Angel City's been inconsistent—two draws in their last three suggest they're finding their rhythm, while Spirit just put four past North Carolina but also dropped one to San Diego. The form lines tell a story of two teams trending different ways heading into the season.

Key storylines:

- **A. Sentnor and C. Emslie** will need to spark Angel City's attack at home; the midfield pairing of **A. Borges and N. Martin** sets the tempo
- Spirit's back line anchored by **T. McKeown and R. Bernal** faces a test from Angel City's width, with **G. Thompson and E. Sams** pushing the flanks
- **L. Santos and H. Hershfelt** pulling strings in Spirit's midfield could exploit space if Angel City commits forward

Expected lineups:

- **Angel City FC**: A. Anderson, E. Shores, S. Gorden, E. Sams, G. Thompson, A. Borges, N. Martin, T. M. Suarez, C. R. Lageyre, C. Emslie, A. Sentnor
- **Washington Spirit**: S. MacIver, G. Carle, T. McKeown, R. Bernal, L. Di Guglielmo, T. Rodman, L. Santos, H. Hershfelt, P. Metayer, E. Morgan, S. Cantore

Prediction:

**2-2 draw** — Spirit's form gives them an edge, but Angel City won't fold at home. Expect goals both ways. ⚽

**Santos is desperate to stop the bleeding** — they've won just once in five and lost three straight at home. Guadalajara, meanwhile, are steadier but still searching for consistency. 🔥

Santos have conceded 7 goals in their last three outings, a genuinely alarming stat. Guadalajara are unbeaten in their last two after that rough patch, so they'll smell blood here.

Key storylines:

- **C. Acevedo** and the Santos backline need to tighten up or this could get ugly fast
- **F. González** leads Guadalajara's press and will be hunting loose balls in midfield
- **D. González** is Santos' attacking heartbeat — he's got to create early or the hosts fold

Expected lineups:

- **Santos Laguna**: C. Acevedo, E. Echeverría, F. Sánchez, F. Pardo, K. Picon, E. Bullaude, F. Villalba, S. Mariscal, R. Sordo, L. Di Yorio, D. González
- **CD Guadalajara**: R. Rangel, L. Romo, J. Castillo, M. Tapias, F. González, B. González, D. Campillo, D. Aguirre, R. Alvarado, A. González, E. Alvarez

**Guadalajara 2–0 Santos**. The hosts' fragile defence meets Guadalajara's uptick in form — a slim lean towards the visitors. 📊

**Seattle's in freefall — down five straight — but the Cascadia Cup waits for no one.** Vancouver's hovering just above .500 and heads to the Emerald City looking to capitalize on a Sounders side that's forgotten how to win. 🔥

The hosts are desperate for a reset after getting picked apart by top-tier opposition, while the Whitecaps have steadied the ship with draws and a recent win. Both teams are absolutely ravaged by injury — Seattle's missing offensive depth and key midfielders, Vancouver's backline is paper-thin — so expect a scrappy, low-flow affair.

Key storylines:

- **Seattle's search for a win:** The Sounders haven't tasted victory in five matches; even at home, they're limping through this stretch.
- **Vancouver's balanced form:** The Whitecaps' 1-2-2 run shows signs of stability compared to Seattle's collapse — a road win here would be huge.
- **Injury carnage everywhere:** Both sides are fielding makeshift XIs; O. D. Rosario and T. Müller become more valuable in a chaotic midfield.

Expected lineups:

- **Seattle Sounders FC**: A. Thomas, N. Tolo, J. Ragen, S. Hawkins, K. Kossa-Rienzi, J. Ferreira, S. Brunell
- **Vancouver Whitecaps**: Y. Takaoka, T. Johnson, M. Laborda, N. Djordjevic, A. Cubas, J. Badwal, R. Gauld

Prediction:

**1-1 draw.** Both offenses are too thin to finish cleanly; expect a gritty stalemate that does nothing for either side's momentum.

**Tijuana's on a tear, and Cruz Azul just got punished by Atlante at home** — this is the kind spot where form hits different. 🔥

Tijuana undefeated in five with three wins, clicking on both ends. Cruz Azul mixed bag: beat Puebla and San Luis but lost to Atlante, now without **A. Morales** and needing to steady the ship in hostile territory.

Key storylines:

- **Tijuana's defensive wall** has conceded just once in five; can **R. Árciga** and the midfield shut down **O. Campos** and a Cruz Azul attack searching for rhythm?
- **D. Abreu** leading the line for Tijuana — if he stays clinical, the hosts could run away with this 🎯
- Cruz Azul's **5-4-1 shape** is compact but vulnerable to transitions; **I. Rivero** and **I. Tona** on the wings could feast on space

Expected lineups:

- **Club Tijuana**: A. Rodríguez, P. N. Ortíz, J. Porozo, R. Fernández, R. Árciga, I. Rivero, A. Preciado, D. Abreu
- **Cruz Azul**: K. Mier, W. Ditta, J. Orozco, A. Garcia, C. Rodríguez, A. Palavecino, O. Campos, O. Ebere

Prediction:

**Tijuana 2–1 Cruz Azul**

Home form, momentum, and Cruz Azul's defensive tweaks without Morales give the edge to the hosts.

**Gnistan's rolling hot, but Ilves own the recent script** — this H2H tells the real story, and it's all Tampere. 🔥

Gnistan are buzzing with 3 wins in their last 5, though that 0-1 loss to KuPS stung. Ilves have been messier (2W-1D-2L), but they've got **Gnistan's number** in head-to-heads, holding a 4-1 edge over the last seven meetings.

- **IF Gnistan's attacking trio** — A. Akinyemi, D. Pérez, and A. Atarah will need to click against a Ilves back line anchored by **V. Kumpu** and **M. Rale**
- **Ilves' midfield control**: **O. Multala** and **S. Baranov** could dictate tempo if Gnistan's press doesn't find teeth early
- **Set-piece battle** — both sides lean on transitions; **G. Europaeus** and **J. Kanga** will be key outlets

- **IF Gnistan**: O. Lyberopoulos, R. Gnanou, A. Jouhi, B. Dahlström, A. Obileye, G. Europaeus, O. Hannula, A. Akinyemi, D. Pérez
- **Ilves**: F. Krkalić, V. Kumpu, M. Rale, S. Väisänen, O. Multala, J. Kanga, J. Kilo, R. Riski, T. Hytönen

Prediction:

**1-1 draw**. Gnistan's form is sharp, but Ilves' head-to-head dominance and home dressing-room vibes give them the slight edge — though not enough to shake free. Coin flip points it.

**Cluj's hunting for back-to-back wins, but Arad's stubborn streak could ruin the party.** Home advantage looks tasty here, though these two have a chaotic history. 🔴

Cluj are **2-1-2 in their last five** with a convincing home win over Botoșani, while Arad keep drawing their way through life — three stalemates in five matches. The visitors haven't won in ages, but they also don't lose easy.

Key storylines:

- **FC Universitatea Cluj** need rhythm at home after that midweek drubbing by Brann; this is a golden chance to stack wins
- **UTA Arad's** defensive shape (three draws in five) suggests they'll pack the midfield and make Cluj work for space
- **P. Pinho** and **A. Aliev** will be crucial for Cluj's attacking flow; Arad's **R. Odada** and **S. Mino** have to keep it tight

- **FC Universitatea Cluj**: S. Lefter, I. Cristea, D. Codrea, A. Chipciu, A. Friday, O. Bic, P. Pinho, A. Aliev, D. Nistor, I. Macalou, A. Trică

**Cluj 2-0 Arad** — home side's slight edge, Arad's form suggests they'll nick a point at best but not enough to stop the hosts. ⚽

**Tuscan derby gets spicy in the Coppa Italia** — Pisa and Empoli collide in a round 32 showdown that's part midseason buildup, part local bragging rights. 🔥

Pisa are riding momentum after hammering Bologna 4-1 away, though they've stumbled at home to lower-league Pro Vercelli. Empoli are stuck in draw hell (three of their last five), but squeezed past Virtus Entella to stay alive in this competition.

Key storylines:

- **Pisa's away form vs Empoli's sluggish attack** — the visitors have the sharper edge after that Bologna demolition, but Empoli's neutral fixture mindset could neutralize them
- **Set-piece chaos incoming** — both teams running three-at-the-back setups means corners and free-kicks become currency
- **H. W. Meister and S. Shpendi as the creative flashpoints** — watch these two dictate tempo and transition speed

Expected lineups:

- **Pisa**: Šemper, Canestrelli, Caracciolo, Bozhinov, Angori, Calabresi, Aebischer, Akinsanmiro, Vural, Moreo, Meister
- **Empoli**: Perisan, Curto, Indragoli, Tosto, Bembnista, Belardinelli, Saporiti, Yepes, Shpendi, Popov, Campaniello

Prediction:

**Pisa 2–1 Empoli**. Pisa's recent spark edges out Empoli's draw-prone displays. 🎯

**Spartak are rolling, Septemvri are in freefall** — one team's hunting a fifth win in five, the other's desperate to avoid a fifth straight loss. 🔴

Spartak's picked up three dubs and a draw over their last four; Septemvri have leaked nine goals in their last three outings and haven't won since the season kicked off. The home fixture, the form gap, and the H2H record all point one way.

- **Spartak's attack** keeps finding the net with **R. Sousa** and **Á. Gomes** linking up in midfield, while **G. Stojanovski** leads the line
- **Septemvri's defense** is bleeding goals — **V. Ivanov** and **B. Stoichkov** will have their hands full against a sharp Varna outfit
- **Home advantage** at Stadion Spartak has been a fortress; Spartak are 2-0 there already this season

- **FK Spartak Varna**: P. Victor, B. Ivanov, T. Marinov, A. Granchov, D. V. Juan, J. Lopes, D. Yordanov
- **FK Septemvri Sofia**: V. Ivanov, B. Stoichkov, K. Onashchi, M. Hristov, B. Tomovski, S. Wade, A. Liberal

Prediction:

**Spartak 3–0 Septemvri**. Septemvri's leaky backline meets a Spartak side in form at home — this should be a rout. 💪

**Sassuolo's form is frankly alarming—three losses in five—but the Coppa Italia opener against lower-league Cesena should be a chance to hit reset.** Cesena's rolling, though; they've won three of their last five and shipped no goals in a pair of those wins. 🔴

**Brøndby roll in as heavy favorites**, but Sønderjyske won't make this easy — the visitors have been a proper bogey side historically. 🔵

**Häcken are heavy favorites here, and honestly, it shows.** Halmstad's form is genuinely dire — four losses in five — while Häcken at least look functional at home with a draw against AIK and a 1-1 with Kalmar. 🔵

Häcken's attack hasn't been clinical (three goals in five), but Halmstad's defense is leaking badly (six conceded in their last three). This feels like the kind of fixture where the better team gets a comfortable W.

Key storylines:
